pre.title: Outcome of Board Meeting
pre.subtype: 70% stake in Belgian CAR-T biotech ACTx via Dutch subsidiary for EUR 48Mn
pre.summary: Mankind Pharma's board approved raising its investment limit in its Dutch subsidiary to EUR 50Mn, which will invest EUR 48Mn in instalments to buy 70% of Armed Cell Therapeutics B.V., a Belgian CAR-T cancer therapy developer. A definitive agreement has been signed, and the deal is paid in cash.
positives: Gives entry into next-generation CAR-T cancer therapies and an innovation pipeline, diversifying beyond the domestic formulations business
Majority control (70%) with experienced founders and R&D teams in the US and EU
Cash outlay is staged in instalments and is small next to the size of a large listed pharma company
negatives: Early-stage, pre-revenue R&D asset; no stated turnover and high clinical and technology risk
Cash outflow of EUR 48Mn with a long, uncertain payback and likely ongoing funding needs
Moves into a field outside the company's core domestic business
amounts: EUR 48Mn investment in ACTx (euro, not USD): 48 USD mn
EUR 50Mn aggregate investment limit in Mankind Netherlands (euro): 50 USD mn
open_questions: Valuation of ACTx and its financials, including cash burn and further funding obligations
Instalment schedule and any milestone or closing conditions
Expected completion timeline and the host-country approvals needed
Stage of the clinical programmes, and the cost and time to commercialisation

results.title: Press Release
results.subtype: Q2 & H1 FY27 results with strong revenue, EBITDA and PAT growth
results.summary: Mankind Pharma reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 4,338 crore (up 17.3% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,175 crore (up 27.2%) and PAT of INR 716 crore (up 37.7%). EBITDA margin improved 210 bps to 27.1%, with domestic ex-consumer healthcare up 15.9% and exports up 32.7%.
positives: EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 27.1%; PAT up 37.7% YoY and margin up 240 bps to 16.5%
Revenue up 17.3% YoY, with exports up 32.7% and domestic ex-consumer healthcare up 15.9%
Domestic secondary sales grew 15.7% against IPM at 14.2%, with more brands above Rs 50 crore and Rs 100 crore
negatives: Consumer healthcare revenue grew only 1.2% YoY and fell 7.0% QoQ on slower category offtake and regional impact
Gross margin fell 60 bps QoQ to 72.2%
open_questions: Management guidance for the rest of FY27 is not given
Reasons behind the profit jump, such as one-offs or other income, are not detailed
Financial terms and impact of the Armed Cell Therapeutics acquisition are not stated
Cash flow and debt position are not given

results.title: Investor Presentation
results.subtype: Q2 & H1 FY27 investor presentation, strong growth in revenue and profit
results.summary: Mankind Pharma's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.3% YoY to Rs 4,338 crore, with EBITDA up 27.2% to Rs 1,175 crore and PAT up 37.7% to Rs 716 crore. EBITDA margin improved 210 bps to 27.1%, led by domestic growth of 15.9% (ex-CH) and exports growth of 32.7%.
positives: Revenue up 17.3% YoY and PAT up 37.7% YoY, with operating leverage
EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 27.1%; gross margin up 90 bps
Exports grew 32.7% and domestic ex-CH grew 15.9%, with 1.2x volume outperformance to IPM
Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.6x; acquisition of Armed Cell Therapeutics adds CAR-T R&D capability
negatives: Consumer Healthcare grew only 1.2% YoY and fell 7.0% QoQ; OTC growth muted
Net debt remains at about Rs 2,639 crore on the chart
amounts: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations: 4338 ₹ crore
open_questions: Price and size of the Armed Cell Therapeutics acquisition
Forward guidance and the one-time labour code impact amount
Reasons for the rise in the PAT margin beyond operations, such as tax or other income
Full details of cash flow and net debt, since the extracted chart text is garbled
